title: Check yourself: parallelizing tasks with ForkJoinPool

questions.stem: A ForkJoinPool of parallelism 2 runs two consumer tasks that each call `orders.take()` on a LinkedBlockingQueue. A producer task that puts the orders is submitted to the same pool after them. What happens?

options.text: The producer runs and both consumers get their orders, since a take() on that queue waits in a way the pool notices and covers with a spare worker
options.says: the Reference lists the blocking queues' take() among the waits for which the pool adds a worker (ran on 21 and 25; this exact case ran too: 3 pool threads)

options.text: The producer stays queued and both consumers keep waiting, since a take() on that queue keeps its worker for as long as the take waits
options.says: some JDK waits, Condition.await() and the blocking queues among them, already block through managedBlock, so the pool adds a worker

options.text: The producer runs and both consumers get their orders, since the pool adds a worker for a queued task that has waited past the keep-alive time
options.says: the keep-alive time is how long an idle worker lives; the pool adds a worker for a managed wait, not for a task that has waited in the queue

options.text: The producer stays queued and both consumers keep waiting, since a pool of parallelism 2 keeps to two threads while its tasks wait
options.says: a pool can have more threads than its parallelism while workers are blocked in managed waits

origin.section: A Worker That Blocks Is Lost to the Pool, Unless It Blocks Through managedBlock()

questions.stem: A nightly job runs `pool.execute(new RebuildShard(n))` for shards 0 to 7, where RebuildShard is a RecursiveAction, then waits until the pool is idle and logs "rebuild done". Shard 5's compute() throws a NullPointerException. What does the night's log show?

options.text: "rebuild done" and nothing about shard 5, since the exception is kept in the task object that the job never joins
options.says: execute returns nothing; the exception stays in the task until someone joins it, and here nobody does

options.text: "rebuild done" and a stack trace for shard 5, since the worker passes a task's exception to its uncaught-exception handler
options.says: that happens to a Runnable given to execute; a ForkJoinTask keeps its exception

options.text: No "rebuild done", since the exception is thrown to the job's thread when it waits for the pool to be idle
options.says: waiting for the pool to go idle does not rethrow a task's exception; only joining that task does

options.text: No "rebuild done", since the exception is thrown to the job's thread from the execute call for shard 5
options.says: execute returns at once, before the task runs, and never throws the task's exception

origin.section: A Failure Reaches the Caller Through invoke() or join(), and execute() Keeps It in the Task

questions.stem: A command-line tool creates `ForkJoinPool pool = new ForkJoinPool(6)`. Then, on its main thread, it calls `task.fork()` on each of six RecursiveTasks, and afterwards `join()` on each. Where does each fork() put its task?

options.text: In the pool the tool made, since fork() picks the pool that was created most recently
options.says: fork() goes to the pool of the current task; from a thread that is no pool's worker, that is the common pool

options.text: In the common pool, since fork() hands a task from a non-worker thread to that pool
options.says: the main thread is no pool's worker, so fork() schedules the task in ForkJoinPool.commonPool(), whatever pools exist

options.text: In no pool at all, since fork() called on the main thread runs the task right there
options.says: fork() schedules the task; called outside a pool, it schedules it in the common pool

options.text: In no pool at all, since join() later runs each task on the thread that waits for it
options.says: fork() has already scheduled each task in the common pool before any join()

origin.section: invoke() Waits for One Task; submit() Lets Them All Run

questions.stem: A REST endpoint handles each request with `return new ForkJoinPool(8).invoke(new Aggregate(rows));` and never shuts the pool down. The service gets about 30 requests a second, all day. What happens to it?

options.text: Nothing that lasts, since each pool and its workers are garbage-collected once the request returns
options.says: an unclosed pool keeps its workers alive after its last task; the 800 live threads show they are not reclaimed when the request returns

options.text: Nothing that lasts, since pool workers are daemon threads and end with the request that used them
options.says: daemon only means they don't keep the JVM from exiting; they outlive the request

options.text: Its thread count climbs, since a pool's idle workers end more slowly than new pools start more of them
options.says: an unclosed pool keeps its workers after its last task; at 30 pools a second they pile up faster than idle workers end

options.text: Its thread count climbs, since a pool's idle workers stay parked until another task for that pool arrives
options.says: idle workers do end after a keep-alive time without new tasks; the trouble is that they end more slowly than new pools start them

origin.section: A Pool You Create Keeps Its Threads Until You Close It
